column1: # `function` skills are the one part of the curriculum that is not about a
# particular language. "Order food or a drink politely" is the same real-world
# capability in Spanish, English or Greek, and the slug naming it is already
# language-neutral — only the label a learner reads is not. So the slug, the
# description and the prerequisite graph live here, once, and each
# content/<tag>/skills.tsv contributes the label and the level for its own
# This is what stops a second direction forking the curriculum. core-en does
# not restate that handle-add-on follows order-food-drink; it says how English
# spells them. A function row whose slug is missing here fails the build.
# Not every language covers every capability, and that is legitimate: a
# language may be authored up to A1 while this file reaches B1. Coverage is a
# per-language question, so absence is never an error here.
# A description here has to be neutral, which is a real constraint and not a
# style note. `confirm-with-a-tag` was authored as "with ¿verdad? or ¿no?" —
# true, useful, and no help at all to a learner of English, who needs "right?"
# or "isn't it?". So the neutral description is the default and a language may
# override it in its own skills.tsv when it can say something more concrete.
# An override that merely restates this column is rejected, or the default
# Ordering food in Spanish and ordering food in English are two things to be
# good at, and mastery of one is not evidence of the other. What is shared is
